title: You thought it was just about money.
paragraphs:
You thought it was just about money.
It’s not.
It’s about what owns your soul.

Because that man holding the scale…
that’s not just famine.
That’s you—when life becomes a transaction with God.
And here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

Why does it feel like no matter how much you give, strive, or earn…
it’s never enough?

Why does your heart still feel empty
even when your hands are full?
Let’s go deeper.

Because the black horse doesn’t just ride in the end times—
it rides in quiet places.

In hidden motives.
In silent compromises.
In the secret belief that “If I just do more… God will accept me.”
That’s where the weight begins.
You start measuring everything.

Your worth.
Your obedience.
Your prayers.
Your failures.
And suddenly, your relationship with God becomes a scale.

“I did good today… maybe He loves me more.”
“I failed again… maybe He’s disappointed.”
That’s not devotion.
That’s bondage.
And it’s heavier than famine.

Because physical hunger can break your body—
but this kind of hunger?
It breaks your identity.
Listen carefully.

The Bible says in Revelation 6:5–6:
“When he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, ‘Come!’ And I looked, and behold, a black horse! And its rider had a pair of scales in his hand. And I heard what seemed to be a voice… saying, ‘A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius…’”

A full day’s wage…
for barely enough to survive.
This is scarcity.
But not just physical.
Spiritual.
Because sin always creates imbalance.

It promises satisfaction—
but delivers emptiness.

It whispers freedom—
but produces chains you can’t see.

Some scholars interpret this passage as literal famine during the end times.
Others see it also as a symbol of economic oppression and injustice.
But don’t miss this—

At its core, it reveals what happens
when humanity tries to live apart from God.
Everything becomes expensive.

Peace? Costly.
Joy? Rare.
Purpose? Fragile.
And righteousness?
Impossible to earn.
That’s the part we don’t want to admit.

You can’t outwork your sin.
You can’t outbalance your guilt.
You can’t tip the scale in your favor.
Because the standard isn’t “better than others.”
It’s perfection.
And the Bible is clear:

Romans 3:23 —
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
All.
No exceptions.

That means every hidden thought…
every secret compromise…
every quiet pride…
It all adds weight to the scale.
And here’s the breaking point—

If your salvation depends on your balance…
you’re already bankrupt.
But wait.
Because this is where everything changes.
This is where the Gospel steps in.
Not with more weight.
But with a cross.
Jesus didn’t come to help you balance the scale.
He came to destroy it.

2 Corinthians 5:21 says:
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”
Read that again.

He took your imbalance…
your failure…
your shame…
And He placed it on Himself.
At the cross, the scales didn’t tip—
They shattered.
Completely.
Because Jesus paid a price you could never afford.

Not with silver.
Not with effort.
Not with performance.
But with His blood.

1 Peter 1:18–19 says:
“You were not redeemed with perishable things such as silver or gold… but with the precious blood of Christ.”
That means this:
You are not accepted because you’re good.
You are accepted because He is.
You are not saved because you earned it.
You are saved because He finished it.
“It is finished.” — John 19:30
That’s not just a statement.
That’s your freedom.
So why are you still holding the scale?

Why are you still measuring yourself
when Jesus already declared you redeemed?
This is the moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “get better.”
Now.
Drop the scale.
Let go of the exhausting need to prove yourself.
Repent—not just of sin, but of self-reliance.
Turn to Jesus.

Not halfway.
Not casually.
Fully.

Because He is not just the answer to famine—
He is the Bread of Life.

John 6:35 —
“I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst.”
You don’t need more.
You need Him.
Right now, where you are—
Say it in your heart:

“Jesus, I surrender.
I can’t fix myself.
I can’t earn this.
I need You.”
And He will meet you there.
Not with condemnation.
But with grace.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
And if this stirred something deep in you…

From scarcity to salvation—
because Jesus already paid what you never could.
